articles.title: Glimpses into lives of Roman suburbanites in Bath revealed in rare finds
articles.description: Exclusive: Restoration work at Bath Assembly Rooms unearths Roman ditches containing pottery, coins and fragments of a military helmet The restoration of a Georgian building in Bath once frequented by Jane Austen has unexpectedly provided a tantalising glimpse into the life of the city’s Roman suburbanites. A network of Roman ditches containing pottery, coins, glassware and a fragment of a military helmet has been found beneath Bath Assembly Rooms in the north of the city. Continue reading...

articles.title: How opencast mining risks reawakening dormant geological faults
articles.description: New study finds subsidence caused by groundwater extraction can take place as far as 20km from site of mine The impact of opencast mining goes far beyond the edge of the pit. Studies of an opencast coalmine in western Germany show that opencast mining triggered extensive subsidence in the surrounding area and re-activated dormant geological faults. Underground mines are often associated with ground subsidence, but less is known about the risks associated with opencast mines. Researchers from the GFZ Helmholtz Centre for Geosciences in Potsdam, Germany, studied satellite data and geological field measurements from the area around the opencast Rhenish coalfields, between Aachen and Cologne. Continue reading...

articles.title: Tree vaccines and gene-edited butterflies among biotechnology projects funded by UK ‘invention agency’
articles.description: Exclusive: The tax-funded brainchild of Dominic Cummings hopes to find ways to speed up wild species’ evolution Vaccines for ash trees, skin treatments for newts and gene-edited swallowtail butterflies are among 14 tax-funded projects from the UK’s “invention agency” aiming to accelerate nature’s ability to adapt to the climate crisis. The £54m accelerated adaptation programme from the UK’s Advanced Research and Invention Agency (Aria) – a public body that funds high-risk, high-reward tech projects – aims to investigate applications of biotechnology that can speed up wild species’ evolution and help them to adapt to new threats such as global warming and disease. Continue reading...

articles.title: From paleo to intermittent fasting: are any diets actually good for us? - podcast

source.name: Presented by Ian Sample; produced by Joshan Chana; sound design by Joel Cox; executive producer Ellie Bury

articles.description: As diet trends proliferate on social media, it can be hard to work out which are backed by science and which should be ignored. From paleo to keto, raw food to intermittent fasting, each attracts a tribe of ardent followers. Now Daniel Lieberman, professor of biological sciences at Harvard University, has written a book to try to cut through the noise. In Fed Up, he uses his background as an evolutionary anthropologist to scrutinise the evidence, turning himself into a guinea pig in the process and trying various diets. In this podcast, he tells Ian Sample which one has remained part of his routine Order Fed Up from the Guardian Bookshop Support the Guardian: theguardian.com/sciencepod Continue reading...

articles.title: US judge declines to block transfer of wildlife refuge land to Musk’s SpaceX
articles.description: Environmental groups vow to continue opposition to deal that would expand site for Elon Musk rocket company A federal judge on Monday refused to block the Trump administration from giving SpaceX more than 700 acres of wildlife refuge as part of a land swap in Texas, while environmental groups vowed to continue their legal challenge. US district judge Fernando Rodriguez Jr declined the plaintiffs’ request for a preliminary injunction to prevent the parcel exchange, saying they failed to prove it would worsen ecological risks to a Gulf coast region already transformed by billionaire Elon Musk’s rocket operations. Continue reading...

articles.title: Discovery of new Australian stick insect species reveals case of mistaken identity
articles.description: New study describes two species, Anchiale robusta and Anchiale mabiensis, both found in far north Queensland Follow our Australia news live blog for latest updates Sign up for climate and environment editor Adam Morton’s free Clear Air newsletter here Two new large stick insect species have been identified by Australian researchers, in a discovery they say illustrates how little we still understand about insect diversity. The two species, both found in far north Queensland, are described in a study published in Austral Entomology. Sign up for climate and environment editor Adam Morton’s free Clear Air newsletter here Continue reading...

articles.title: ‘Jaw-dropping’ El Niño bursts through temperature record months before peak
articles.description: ‘Godzilla-level’ phenomenon is supercharging the climate crisis and will have a huge impact on communities across the world The “jaw-dropping” El Niño currently heating up the planet has burst through the highest temperature ever recorded for the phenomenon, several months before its expected peak. The latest data shows the temperature rise at the heart of El Niño in the Pacific Ocean has now reached 3.05C. That is higher than the 3.02C set in late November 2015, the previous high set in the 150 years of modern records. This temperature is measured against the average of 1991-2020. Continue reading...

articles.title: Trump reportedly to form health funding board that could veto ‘woke’ initiatives
articles.description: President’s latest order expected to bring NIH funding under control of Trump administration to align with agenda Donald Trump’s latest executive order is expected to establish a board responsible for approving National Institutes of Health (NIH) grant funding, marking another attempt by the Trump administration to censor topics that do not align with the president’s agenda. The executive order, reported by outlets including the Washington Post and Politico, was discussed in a meeting on Friday in which senior administration officials accused the NIH of funding “woke” initiatives that went against Trump’s political priorities. Continue reading...

articles.title: Glimpses into lives of Roman suburbanites in Bath revealed in rare finds
articles.description: Exclusive: Restoration work at Bath Assembly Rooms unearths Roman ditches containing pottery, coins and fragments of a military helmet The restoration of a Georgian building in Bath once frequented by Jane Austen has unexpectedly provided a tantalising glimpse into the life of the city’s Roman suburbanites. A network of Roman ditches containing pottery, coins, glassware and a fragment of a military helmet has been found beneath Bath Assembly Rooms in the north of the city. Continue reading...

articles.title: How opencast mining risks reawakening dormant geological faults
articles.description: New study finds subsidence caused by groundwater extraction can take place as far as 20km from site of mine The impact of opencast mining goes far beyond the edge of the pit. Studies of an opencast coalmine in western Germany show that opencast mining triggered extensive subsidence in the surrounding area and re-activated dormant geological faults. Underground mines are often associated with ground subsidence, but less is known about the risks associated with opencast mines. Researchers from the GFZ Helmholtz Centre for Geosciences in Potsdam, Germany, studied satellite data and geological field measurements from the area around the opencast Rhenish coalfields, between Aachen and Cologne. Continue reading...

articles.title: Germany's saviour? How Klopp is looking to turn fortunes around
articles.description: As Jurgen Klopp prepares for his first game as Germany manager, BBC Sport looks at how is trying to turn their fortunes around.

articles.title: Hadjar to stay as Verstappen's Red Bull team-mate for 2027
articles.description: Frenchman Isack Hadjar is to stay at Red Bull as Max Verstappen's team-mate for the 2027 season.

articles.title: Scots recall Kerr & Thomas for World Cup play-offs
articles.description: Sam Kerr and Martha Thomas are named in their first Scotland squad in almost a year for next month's World Cup round one play-offs against the Czech Republic.

articles.title: Jacks stars as England grind out win over Sri Lanka
articles.description: Will Jacks' all-round efforts help England grind out an 89-run victory over Sri Lanka in the first one-day international at Chester-le-Street.

articles.title: From leaving Rangers to La Liga - Scotland is next step for Ure
articles.description: Robbie Ure has made it all the way to Sevilla since failing to break through at Rangers and now a first Scotland cap awaits the striker, writes Tom English.

articles.title: MLS coach sacked after sexist remark to female referee
articles.description: MLS club Columbus Crew sack their reserve team coach after he refused to let go of a female referee's hand and says "don't forget this is a man's game".

articles.title: Pornhub investigated over its age checks
articles.description: The regulator says it has concerns over how the site is relying on third party checks provided by Apple for some users.

articles.title: US criticises Australia's proposed algorithm opt-out laws as 'censorship'
articles.description: Under the draft laws, tech firms face fines if they do not give users the option to switch off algorithms.

articles.title: Will a switch to light speed cut power use at data centres?
articles.description: To save power and add capacity, data centres are switching from copper wires to tech using light.

articles.title: Huge data centres rise at 'China speed' to power its AI ambitions

articles.description: The BBC is in Inner Mongolia where dozen of Chinese data centres are being constructed, as the country aims to lead the world in artificial intelligence.

articles.description: The news comes as part of a "reset" announced by Xbox in July, with 3,600 planned job losses overall.
